title: TCO Layer Optical and Electrical Degradation (HJT)

key_findings.detail:
Under negative bias, Na⁺ ions arriving at the ITO surface cause local reduction:

- Metallic indium (In⁰) is reduced from ITO (In₂O₃·SnO₂) at sites of Na⁺ accumulation
- Metallic indium nanoparticles absorb incident light, reducing optical transmittance through the TCO
- This manifests primarily as **Isc loss** (less light reaching the a-Si:H/c-Si absorber)
- Front-side HJT degradation under negative bias: Isc loss of **53.9% after 800 h**
- [[papers/Wiley-107-890-2-s2.0-85180462440-2024-J-Potential-induced degradation in bifacial silicon heterojunction solar modules: Insights and mitigat.pdf#page=4|Luo et al. (2024), p.4]]

key_findings.claim: Nano-Crack Formation and Ion Penetration (Passivation Loss Mechanism)
key_findings.detail:
SEM and TEM imaging of PID-stressed HJT cells reveals:

- Nano-cracks form at the ITO surface under electrochemical attack
- Na⁺ and OH⁻ groups migrate through nano-cracks into the a-Si:H intrinsic layer
- Na⁺ creates recombination centers at the a-Si:H/c-Si interface
- These recombination centers reduce interface passivation quality (increasing surface SRV)
- This manifests primarily as **FF loss** (increased series/shunt resistance and recombination)
- [[papers/Wiley-251-3004-2-s2.0-85045834850-2018-J-Comprehensive study of potential-induced degradation in silicon heterojunction photovoltaic cell mod.pdf#page=4|Zu et al. (2018), p.4]]

key_findings.claim: Front vs. Rear Side Degradation Signatures
key_findings.detail:
The failure mode differs between front and rear TCO layers:

| Parameter | Front Side (negative bias) | Rear Side |
|-----------|--------------------------|-----------|
| Dominant loss | Isc (optical absorption) | FF (recombination) |
| Pmax loss (800 h) | 53.9% | 40.4% |
| Primary mechanism | Metallic In⁰ formation | Interface passivation loss |

- [[papers/Wiley-107-890-2-s2.0-85180462440-2024-J-Potential-induced degradation in bifacial silicon heterojunction solar modules: Insights and mitigat.pdf#page=5|Luo et al. (2024), p.5]]

Even without voltage bias, moisture alone degrades HJT TCO:

- Water-induced glass corrosion creates NaOH at the glass/EVA/ITO interface
- NaOH chemically attacks ITO, causing structural changes to the TCO layer
- **20% Isc loss** after 500 h of damp heat (85°C, 85% RH) with no applied bias
- Applied negative voltage accelerates this process dramatically
- [[papers/Wiley-251-3004-2-s2.0-85045834850-2018-J-Comprehensive study of potential-induced degradation in silicon heterojunction photovoltaic cell mod.pdf#page=3|Zu et al. (2018), p.3]]

Unlike p-type c-Si PID-s, HJT PID shows very limited reversibility:

- Slight initial recovery followed by a plateau
- Recovery fails because metallic indium formation and nano-crack damage are largely irreversible structural changes
- [[papers/Wiley-107-890-2-s2.0-85180462440-2024-J-Potential-induced degradation in bifacial silicon heterojunction solar modules: Insights and mitigat.pdf#page=7|Luo et al. (2024), p.7]]
